label: First copy step (output orig[1]) in short sequences (L=3-4), gated by token identity, esp. first token e/f
explanation: Fires only at step t = L+1, the first copy step after <DEL> (input = orig[0] fed back, output = orig[1]), and only in very short sequences: L=3 holds ~73% of mass, L=4 ~27%, L=5 a trace, never L>=6. Never fires in the original or delimiter phases or at any other copy step. Within that slot it is sparse and token-dependent: when L=3 and the first token is e or f it fires essentially always (precision ~0.99) and at the highest magnitudes; first tokens h, b, j, 0, n, z fire less often/weaker; the second original token also modulates (e, z, f, b, n raise it; a, u, o, s, p, l suppress it), and digits among the originals reduce firing. Magnitude is largest for L=3 with first token e/f. Looks like a short-sequence position detector thresholded by an additive token-content signal, so a boolean predicate captures most mass (~0.9) but precision is only ~0.5.

scorecard.summary: Graded preference over the current input token (most: e, f, h, b, j, 0; least: t, o, a, i) and the second original token (most: e, f, z, n, b, h; least: o, 2, 3, i); timing cues that raise it most: L=3 & t=4, recall_idx=1, L=4 & t=5.
